title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 39 (Effect of refusal of party to perform promise wholly)

content.overview: Section 39 provides that when a party to a contract has refused to perform, or disabled himself from performing, his promise in its entirety, the promisee may put an end to the contract, unless he has signified, by words or conduct, his acquiescence in its continuance.
content.glance: Refusal or self-disablement from performing the promise in its entirety → promisee may put an end to the contract, unless acquiescence.
content.study: If a party refuses to perform or disables himself from performing his promise in its entirety, the promisee may put an end to the contract, unless he has signified by words or conduct his acquiescence in its continuance. This is the statutory rule on anticipatory breach / renunciation. Current-law framing: establish refusal or self-disablement as to the whole promise; test whether the promisee has acquiesced; if not, the promisee may terminate.

sections.heading: Refusal or self-disablement
sections.body: Party has refused to perform, or disabled himself from performing, his promise in its entirety.

sections.heading: Promisee’s election
sections.body: Promisee may put an end to the contract, unless he has signified by words or conduct his acquiescence in its continuance.

provisions.title: Effect of refusal of party to perform promise wholly

examples.title: Renunciation before performance due
examples.body: A contracts to deliver goods on a future date and then refuses to perform. B may put an end to the contract under s. 39 unless B has acquiesced in its continuance.

hypotheticals.question: Must the promisee terminate immediately?
hypotheticals.analysis: The promisee may put an end to the contract, but if he signifies acquiescence by words or conduct, he cannot later rely on s. 39 to terminate on that ground.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-39
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Any partial shortfall lets the promisee terminate under s. 39.
misconceptions.correction: Section 39 requires refusal or self-disablement from performing the promise in its entirety.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 39 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Establish refusal or self-disablement as to the whole promise. II. Test acquiescence by the promisee. III. Apply election to put an end to the contract. IV. Conclude.
